title: Introduce hybrid-deadline-queue with KV-probe rate-limiter to reduce starvation in continuous-batcher
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a hybrid deadline-aware queue and a KV-probe rate limiter for continuous-batcher to reduce starvation for low-throughput long-sequence requests. No API changes. Runtime flags gated behind feature flag 'hybrid_deadline_v1'.
commits: 4 commits: 1) initial hybrid-deadline queue data structures and tests; 2) integrate KV-probe rate-limiter into admission path; 3) heuristics for slot-fusion and soft-grace windows; 4) docs and telemetry metrics for queue/fairness evaluation.
changed_files_high_level: scheduler/continuous/queue.h, scheduler/continuous/queue.cc, scheduler/continuous/admitter.cc, runtime/kv_probe_rate_limiter.{h,cc}, tests/continuous/queue_test.cc, docs/design/hybrid_deadline_queue.md, telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml, bench/continuous_starvation_scenarios.yml, scripts/ci/flake_retry.sh
description:
Motivation: Continuous-batcher was showing observed starvation for low-throughput long-sequence requests (e.g., multi-turn chat with large KV-cache hits) when high fan-in short requests dominated the batcher. Existing deadline-slotting reduced latency but over-prioritized high-throughput streams, causing tail regressions for some customer workloads. This PR introduces a hybrid-deadline-queue that blends deadline slotted admission with a lightweight fairness credit and a KV-probe rate-limiter that controls how aggressively KV-prefetch/probe-heavy requests can occupy admission slots.

Design summary: - Hybrid deadline queue: requests are assigned a deadline bucket but also accrue an aging fairness credit when they wait. The admission policy prefers earliest deadline but will pick a request with sufficient fairness credit after a soft-grace window to avoid starvation. Credit accrual is proportional to time waited and request weight (tokens * kv_penalty_factor). - KV-probe rate-limiter: a token-bucket style limiter applied at the admission path for requests that request KV-prefetch hints or large KV pin counts. This prevents probe-heavy requests from flooding the admission pipeline during bursts. - Slot fusion heuristics: when the batcher detects a high proportion of long-sequence KV-heavy requests, it enables slot-fusion to allow coalescing compatible KV contexts and reduce redundant probes. The heuristics are conservative and only enable fusion when meeting stability thresholds defined in bench configs. - Telemetry: added per-bucket wait_time, fairness_credit, kv_probe_throttle_rate, and slot_fusion_engagement metrics to validate behavior in Canary and Dedicated.

Implementation notes: - New code lives under scheduler/continuous. The queue implementation is lock-sharded and uses a compact ring for buckets to limit memory churn. We reused existing kernel hints in admitter to keep hot paths minimal. - KV-probe limiter is pluggable via runtime option "kv_probe_limiter_enabled" and tuned with default tokens=50/s per serving instance (bench-derived) with burst=200. - Feature flag: hybrid_deadline_v1 gates behavior; default on for canary, off for older Dedicated until rolled out. - Backward compat: No changes to public APIs; config knobs added to deployment config schema with defaults.

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit tests: queue unit tests cover fairness accrual, soft-grace expiry, and admission ordering. - Integration tests: synthetic contention scenarios that previously reproduced starvation show 3x reduction in median wait for long-sequence KV-heavy requests and negligible impact (<2%) on short-request p95 in our benchmarks. - Perf bench: bench/continuous_starvation_scenarios.yml and a dedicated bench job run in the PR pipeline. CI initially failed a flaky test (tests/continuous/queue_test.cc::GraceCreditExpiry) due to timing sensitivities; added a deterministic tick mock and re-ran CI.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (docs/design/hybrid_deadline_queue.md) - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Bench configs and local run instructions - [x] Telemetry definitions added - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan - [x] Dev notes for SRE on toggling kv_probe_limiter and slot-fusion thresholds

Related work: This complements prior fairshare and deadline-smoothing efforts (see ENG-1789, pr-71234) but takes a different approach by coupling aging credit with deadline buckets and explicitly limiting KV-probe flood behaviour.

How to validate in staging: 1) Enable feature flag hybrid_deadline_v1 on a canary pool. 2) Deploy bench scenario with a 90/10 mix short/long requests with KV hints. 3) Verify telemetry: fairness_credit increases for backlogged long requests and kv_probe_throttle_rate remains below the configured burst over a 10m window. 4) Run the included bench to confirm p95 latency drift <2% and median for long requests improves.

Rollout plan: Canary -> 10% Dedicated -> 100% Dedicated. Provide auto-rollout abort if kv_probe_throttle_rate > 80% sustained for 5m or if p95 short-request latency delta >5% sustained for 10m.

Notes: config names and metrics are intentionally conservative and documented in the design doc; we should avoid aggressive defaults for slot-fusion.
